pr_snapshot.body:
VP8 loop-filter scoring previously revisited the frame once per 16-pixel column. Scan complete rows with Go archsimd on ARM64 and AVX2, reducing cache traffic and x64 return-fence/reduction overhead. Bounded four-row accumulation preserves the original uint32 column semantics; unsupported inputs and backends retain the existing path.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, one thread, six balanced rounds: public scoring improves 1.141× at 720p and 1.181× at 1088p versus main, and beats the old assembly reference by 1.068× and 1.109×. Small and partial-frame cases improve versus main but still trail assembly. Every component sample is allocation-free and checked against an independent scalar oracle. The first ARM whole-codec run is mixed: +0.83% at 60 frames, −2.69% at 300 frames versus main, with both faster and slower pairs and 23 exact output/options controls plus zero allocations. A fresh eight-pair alternating 300-frame confirmation is effectively flat (median −0.314%, six pairs faster and two slower), again with all 23 controls exact and zero allocations; no overall speedup is claimed. Native x64 measurements are pending; component gains are reported separately and retained under the project's performance policy.

Adds numeric-extreme, minimal-span, spare-capacity, overlapping-input, disabled-backend and encoder integration tests, including frame totals above 2³² and wrapped-column fallback. Extends the native x64 harness with the same four public scoring fixtures for assembly/main/current. Refreshes PGO and preserves PR #25's native assembly/libvpx comparisons under benchmarks/baselines. README unchanged.

Validation: full native `go test ./...`, scalar/integration oracles, race/checkptr, purego and SIMD-off tests, required-SIMD AMD64 Rosetta correctness, and format/no-assembly/build-selection/PGO gates all pass. Native libvpx-backed VP8 timing, extended and 720p runtime-transition byte parity also passes (158 tests/subtests, no skips). The integrated ARM scorer matches all 136 measured instructions after address normalization. CI will provide fresh x64 kernel, whole VP8/VP9 and optimized-libvpx results on the exact head.
